title: Backing up school records before the holiday
description: A practical guide for Kenyan schools on protecting student, fee, and staff records before the long break, with simple backup habits that do not need a big budget.
body:
The end of the year is when schools are most exposed. Staff are leaving, offices are being locked, computers sit unattended for weeks, and a year of records is about to be left alone. A theft, a power surge, a fire, or a failed laptop at this point can erase information that took months to collect.

A few simple habits remove most of that risk.

What needs protecting

  • Student records, admissions details, and parent contacts.
  • Assessment results and report cards for the whole year.
  • Fee records, receipts, and reconciliations.
  • Payroll and staff files.
  • Scanned copies of important paper documents.

The simple rule that works

Keep three copies of important data, on two different kinds of storage, with one copy kept off the school premises. A school that keeps everything on one office computer has one copy on one device in one building.

Systems that store records in the cloud already carry much of this protection, because the data is held securely outside the school and does not depend on a single machine.

Remember the Data Protection Act: Student and parent data is personal data. Backups on a staff member's personal flash disk or phone create a privacy risk. Use controlled, secure storage and keep a note of where copies are held.

Control access as people leave

Year-end is also the time to review who has access. Remove or change credentials for staff who are leaving, make sure someone other than one person holds the administrator login, and avoid sharing passwords.

Test that it works

A backup that has never been restored is an assumption. Before the holiday, open a backup copy and confirm the data is complete and readable. Where records are on paper, scan the critical ones.
